summary: Initial triage across all three servers has not confirmed unauthorized access. The shared deploy password has a long-running recurring source consistent with the old monitoring workload; ordinary staff and service logins also match the restored baseline. I found serious exposures including Grafana 8.3.1 and excessive deploy sudo privileges. Investigating and monitoring current activity while preparing fixes that keep staff and scheduled jobs working.

Found a hidden branch in the rental quote endpoint that returns the WordPress database credentials. Three HTTP 200 responses match the credential-bearing response size, including one at 17:01 UTC; normal quotes are much smaller. I preserved the original file, removed the branch, and verified normal quotes still work. Treating the WordPress database credential as compromised; investigating whether it was used on db-01 and whether the branch exists in CI.

The rental-quote disclosure was removed, the WordPress database password rotated on both ends, and the separate weekly-report configuration updated. The exposed DB account is now restricted to web-01; no unauthorized use on db-01 or ci-01 is confirmed. Grafana stayed available behind a canonical-path proxy and rejected later traversal probes. I also removed several root execution paths, restricted backup and release SSH, and verified scheduled releases, archive transfer, the site, and payout reconciliation. Monitoring continues.
